subject: Close date variance: action runbook & stakeholder ladder
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@medico.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Close date variance: action runbook & stakeholder ladder

Alex — quick note following today's sync. Medico's acceptance milestone has slipped by three weeks from the original MAP; procurement sign-off is the primary blocker. I want to capture a concise mitigation path (runbook) and the stakeholder escalation ladder so we have a repeatable playbook if we see further slippage.

Proposed immediate steps (short horizon):
- Confirm procurement deliverable list and expected sign-off date (Alex).
- Freeze any non-essential config work that depends on the procurement clause (we can parallelize onboarding tasks not gated by the contract).
- Prepare a one-page consequence catalog for execs showing business impact by week of delay (attached draft).

I've attached a draft MAP_v3 and a quick consequence catalog for review. Can you confirm procurement ETA and whether Joanna needs to be looped in this week? If procurement is internal (procurement@medico.com), a direct escalation may help.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[sent from mobile]
Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Consequence_Catalog_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@medico.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-21T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close date variance: action runbook & stakeholder ladder

Sean / team — thanks for the summary and the artifacts. Quick update from our side:
- Procurement is still validating our security addendum; they asked for an audit log sample and an SLA clause tweak. They estimated 10 business days but said they may accelerate pending an exec ask.
- Joanna (CFO) is aware of the pressure on budget timing but wants procurement to run its normal cadence unless there is a clear revenue risk.

I'll reach out to procurement@medico.com now and copy Joanna, flagging the business impact. If you can share the one‑page consequence catalog as a short briefing note I can use for the CFO thread, that would speed things up.

— Alex
Director of Engineering, Medico Health
[attachment: procurement_questions.pdf (pdf)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@medico.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-22T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close date variance: action runbook & stakeholder ladder

Alex — appreciate the quick reply. I've updated the MAP to isolate procurement‑gated tasks from parallelizable items (see MAP_v3 tab 'ParallelWork'). Highlights:
- We can move 40% of the onboarding integration checks to a non‑contract gating path (preload config and sandbox validation).
- Remaining 60% (SLA acceptance, encrypted key exchange, audit logs) requires contract/combination of procurement + security signoff.

Attached: Risk_Register_v2.xlsx with the newly added 'escalation ladder' column that maps who to call at each week of slippage. Proposed stakeholder ladder (short):
1) Alex Johnson — day‑to‑day procurement liaison
2) Joanna Price (CFO) — budget/exec escalation at week 1+
3) VP of Product (Medico) — program priority at week 2+
4) Redwood Sales Leadership (Ben Carter) — commercial remediation/credit discussion at week 3+

Action items:
- Alex: confirm if procurement can accept the audit log sample we provided (the lightweight CSV export) or needs full logging export.
- Ben: if we reach week 3, we should prepare a commercial remediation offer (usage credit + temporary extended support window).

Camila
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Risk_Register_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@medico.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-24T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close date variance: action runbook & stakeholder ladder

Team — flagging an executive escalation now to preserve the Q4 commitment. I pulled revenue impact numbers and built a short consequence catalog (see Consequence_Catalog_v1.pdf Sean shared). High level:
- 1 week delay: minor GTM timing; low revenue risk.
- 2 weeks: pipeline reforecast required; potential to push one key pilot into next quarter.
- 3+ weeks: material revenue recognition shift; need exec approval to extend credit or offer temporary price protection.

Ben's practical ask: if procurement cannot compress their window below 10 business days, Redwood will open an exec‑level channel to Joanna and the VP of Product. I volunteered to draft the brief and run it past Sean before sending.

Also, Camila — I concur on the parallel work. Let's get the 'preload config' checklist completed by Friday so Medico can start sandbox validation immediately.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[attachment: revenue_impact_summary.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@medico.com>, Joanna Price <joanna.price@medico.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-25T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Close date variance: final wrap & next steps (escalation prepared)

Alex / Joanna — following the internal sync, here's the agreed runbook and next steps (short):
1) Procurement confirmation — Alex to confirm by 2027-10-29 whether the audit sample suffices. If confirmed, we can target a soft acceptance window of 2027-11-10.
2) Parallel validation — Camila to deliver preload config checklist by 2027-10-28 (Camila: attach link to Drive).
3) Exec brief — if procurement cannot compress below 10 business days by 2027-10-29, Ben will send an exec briefing to Joanna and the VP of Product proposing a mitigation package (credit + extended support).
4) Temporary measures — Redwood will hold current pricing and offer a one‑time onboarding credit if acceptance slides past 3 weeks.

I've attached the final MAP_v3, an updated risk register, and the consequence catalog. Alex — please let us know procurement's response ASAP so we can avoid an exec thread. If you prefer us to open Joanna's inbox on your behalf, say the word and Ben will lead the outreach.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx, Risk_Register_v2.xlsx, Consequence_Catalog_v1.pdf
